summary: Periodic tenant-wide 429 waves when signed-url refreshes coincide with telemetry flush sweeps
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reported recurring 429 throttles that affect a large proportion of their tenant traffic in short waves (~45–90s) during today’s rolling warmup window. Pattern appears correlated with two independent scheduled operations: (A) client-side signed-url refresh processes (many short-lived clients renewing credentials in tight windows) and (B) BrightCart’s nightly telemetry flush (lots of background POSTs to ingestion endpoints).

Impact:
- ~30% of requests from BrightCart receive 429s for short bursts, causing degraded UX for interactive flows (timeouts on chat widgets).
- Incident is customer-visible in prod-us-west and affects both text-generation and embedding routes.

Environment:
- Customer tenant: brightcart-prod (enterprise)
- Deployment: Redwood hosted (dedicated capacity pool for tenant)
- Region: us-west
- Observed during scheduled warmup window: 03:00–03:30 UTC daily

Requested outcome:
- Understand why these short bursts are being counted as tenant-wide quota exhaustion rather than being isolated to background sweep traffic.
- Recommend short-term mitigation and long-term config changes to prevent overlap-induced 429 waves.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs scheduled telemetry flush job that posts ~2000 small payloads concurrently to /v1/ingest with signed-url auth (occurs at 03:05 UTC).
2) Simultaneously, a fleet of client workers perform signed-url refresh and immediately open short-lived streaming sessions to check status (~500 concurrent sessions).
3) Within 10–30s of overlap, platform rate limiter begins returning 429 to interactive and ingest routes for the tenant.
4) Wave persists ~45–90s then subsides as refill window progresses and background sweep finishes.
logs: 2026-03-10T03:05:12Z edge-proxy[ingress] INFO tenant=brightcart req_id=abc123 status=200 path=/v1/ingest size=512
2026-03-10T03:05:14Z rate-limiter WARN tenant=brightcart token_window=short refill_remaining=0 rejected=120
2026-03-10T03:05:16Z edge-proxy[ingress] ERROR tenant=brightcart req_id=def456 status=429 path=/v1/generate reason=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-10T03:06:40Z scheduler INFO job=telemetry-flush completed payloads=1978 duration=95s
comments: Maya Patel (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer opened ticket with console screenshots and a timeline showing 429 peaks matching their telemetry flush. Asked for immediate mitigation during nightly window.
Jeremy Cho (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Requested sample request IDs, edge-proxy access logs, and tenant quota accounting snapshot for 03:00–03:10 UTC.

BrightCart Ops (customer) - 2026-03-11: Provided signed-url refresh cadence (every 60s across 500 workers, default jitter disabled) and telemetry flush job manifest. They can reschedule within 2 hours if needed.

Omar Velasquez (Rate-limiter eng) - 2026-03-11: Noted that refill windows are aligned to epoch boundaries and short-window burst accounting can cause transient tenant-wide depletion when two windows of different traffic classes align. Investigating whether background flushes are being charged to interactive priority lane.
Jeremy Cho (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Implemented temporary rate isolation rule for brightcart-prod to segregate telemetry endpoint into background pool; monitoring for 24h.
BrightCart Ops - 2026-03-12: Confirmed immediate drop in user-facing 429s during nightly run after temporary isolation applied. Observed small number of failed telemetry items retried successfully.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Signed-url refreshes create many short-lived sessions which touch the same per-tenant token bucket accounting as interactive calls because signed-url callbacks include the same route tag — causing simultaneous drains.
Hypothesis B: Telemetry flush uses chunked POSTs that the ingest path tags as 'interactive' due to legacy header; should be counted against background/bulk pool.

Telemetry from console shows refill_remaining reached zero at 03:05:14Z and rejected spikes coincide with scheduler completion times. Token accounting dump shows large debit entries labeled 'ingest' but with weight equivalent to interactive tokens.
Edge-proxy analysis: keepalive count surged due to zero jitter refresh; connection churn also increased NAT mapping reuse, possibly causing multiple token attributions per logical job run.
Related config: Customer uses dedicated pool with default burst pool sharing; no explicit route-based isolation configured prior to mitigation.
root_cause: Background telemetry flushes and high-frequency signed-url refreshes were both being debited against the tenant's shared burst token window and, because both traffic classes aligned with the same refill epoch, the short-window refill was exhausted causing tenant-wide 429s.
resolution:
Applied a two-part mitigation and follow-ups:
- Short-term: created a temporary split in rate pools for brightcart-prod: /v1/ingest routed to background-burst pool with separate refill cadence; interactive routes kept on interactive-pool. This reduced user-facing 429s immediately.
- Medium-term: recommended customer enable jitter for signed-url refresh (randomized 30–90s) and move telemetry flush to staggered batches or to a dedicated background route.
- Long-term: engineering to deploy a console UI control for per-route burst isolation and a safeguard that refuses to tag large scheduled jobs as interactive.

Customer impact after mitigation: user-facing 429 rate dropped from ~30% to <1% during next scheduled run. Telemetry retries increased transiently but completed.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-12590: Add route-level burst pool UI and API (owner: rate-limiter team)
OPS-4491: Create KB entry for customers on 'Signed-url refresh jitter and telemetry batching' (owner: Solutions Engineering)
SRE-3322: Schedule a config rollout to make background ingestion auto-isolate on dedicated pools for enterprise tenants (owner: SRE)
CS-210: Reach out to BrightCart in 48 hours to confirm stability and discuss best-practices adoption (owner: Customer Success)
Customer action: BrightCart to enable jitter for signed-url refresh and adjust telemetry flush to 10 parallel batches spread across 10 minutes.
notes: This ticket highlights a common failure mode when scheduled background traffic and frequent credential refreshes are not isolated by route or priority. Recommend updating onboarding docs for enterprise tenants to include default isolation recipes.
